chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked him about salat (prayer) in the month of Ramadan, so he said: Thirteen rak'ahs, including the witr and the two rak'ahs of dawn after fajr. That is how the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to pray, and I likewise pray in that manner; and if it had been good, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم would not have left it.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer) being asked about in Ramadan
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: fajr, the dawn time after which the two rak'ahs are mentioned
key_terms.الْوِتْرُ: the witr prayer included within the total
key_terms.ثَلَاثَ عَشْرَةَ رَكْعَةً: thirteen units of prayer mentioned as the total
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم whose practice is cited as proof
key_terms.رَكْعَتَا الصُّبْحِ: the two rak'ahs associated with dawn
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan as the time under discussion

ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs of salat (prayer) are reported in this hadith for the month of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding salat (prayer) in the month of Ramadan, stating a practice of thirteen rak'ahs including witr and the two rak'ahs of dawn. It grounds the ruling in the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and presents his precedent as proof in matters of worship.
